title: Machine-learning variable selection supports 90-day heart-failure risk prediction
summary: In 3,189 patients hospitalized for heart failure, machine-learning variable selection supported a logistic model for 90-day acute-heart-failure readmission or death. LASSO selection and logistic regression yielded a reported AUC of 0.760, compared with 0.744 for logistic regression alone. This single-centre retrospective analysis used internal cross-validation; external performance and benefits from model-guided care were not tested.
ai_technology: LASSO; gradient boosting; random forest; support vector machine

source_review.scope: Primary full paper Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata;reviewed 2026-11-21.

evidence.tested: Retrospective single-centre 3,189-patient analysis with four-fold variable-selection cross-validation and LR comparator.
evidence.unknown: External validation, prospective performance and benefits of model-guided care remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Four-fold ML selection compared LASSO, GBM, RF, SVM.
